title: Runtime stability & upgrade safeguards: semantic version policy and rollout runbooks
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Purpose: define a clear and predictable semantic versioning policy for the Redwood serving runtime plus operational rollout safeguards so customers can trust in-place upgrades and opt-in LTS channels. This ticket captures the versioning model, deprecation cadence, compatibility guarantees, automated upgrade tooling expectations, and the runbook for rollouts and emergency rollbacks.
summary: Canonical semver & upgrade guardrails for runtime artifacts (server binary, grpc/http API contract, model-KV schemas, and administrative control-plane APIs). Focus on minimizing customer disruption and enabling automated safe upgrades for Dedicated/Private deployments.
policy_overview: 1) Version schema: MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH (runtime). MAJOR++ for breaking changes to public RPC/API wire contracts or default behavior that may change inference results in customer-visible ways. MINOR++ for additive, backward-compatible features and opt-in performance improvements. PATCH++ for bug fixes, security patches, and non-behavioral changes.
breaking_change_definition: A breaking change is any alteration that will cause a previously working client, SDK, or configuration to fail, change output semantics beyond documented tolerances, or alter persisted KV/cache formats without migration tooling. Examples: removal of an RPC field, changes to default tokenizer mapping for existing pinned model, incompatibility in on-disk cache format.
deprecation_policy: Deprecation must be announced in-code (deprecation header in responses & admin API), release notes, and via console. Minimum deprecation window: 90 days for MINOR->MAJOR transition; 180 days if customers can pin to on-disk formats or binary artifacts (Dedicated/Private). Deprecation header format: X-Redwood-Deprecation: v<deprecated_version>; removal_target: v<target_major>; note: <short-reason>; migration: <link>
lts_channel_policy: We maintain two LTS channels: lts-stable (older, 12-month support) and lts-current (recommended, 6-month support). LTS releases are MAJOR or MINOR releases marked with 'lts' metadata. Security & critical bugfixes are cherry-picked to all active LTS channels; features are not backported unless explicitly requested and approved.
compatibility_guarantees: - Wire-level compatibility: within same MAJOR, runtime guarantees request/response JSON schemas will be supported for MINOR and PATCH bumps. - Binary compatibility: we guarantee in-process plugin extension points remain stable across PATCH and MINOR where possible; breaking ABI requires MAJOR. - Persistence compatibility: on-disk KV/cache schema changes require a documented migration path or dual-read fallback for one full release cycle.
compatibility_testing: We will add a 'compat-suite' matrix that runs against every candidate release: SDK smoke tests, API contract tests (golden request/response fixtures), on-disk migration tests, and end-to-end performance regression checks. The matrix runs on combinations of previous two MAJOR versions and the new candidate.
rollout_gates: Gates for progressive rollout: 1) Unit/integration checks pass 2) Contract tests pass against previous major fixtures 3) Canary: 5% traffic for 24h with elevated telemetry 4) Gradual increase to 25% for 48h 5) Production ramp to 100% unless predefined error/latency thresholds breach. Gate metrics: error_rate (>=5xx) delta > 0.5% absolute, p95 latency regression > 20%, token loss or generation drift flagged by eval set regressions.
rollback_triggers: Automatic rollback if any gate metric breaches AND absolute impact exceeds our safety threshold (see rollout_gates). Manual rollback can be triggered by SRE/Oncall for severe customer-visible failures. Rollbacks must have a postmortem linked and a follow-up fix ticket.
upgrade_tooling: Deliverables: 1) 'rwu' CLI (redwood-upgrade) to validate binary compatibility and run preflight checks on Dedicated/Private clusters. 2) Control-plane API endpoints to orchestrate canary percentages and schedule automated rollbacks. 3) Migration helpers (one-shot jobs) for on-disk KV schema upgrades, with dry-run mode and verification checks.
cli_preflight_checks: rwu preflight will verify: cluster health, schema versions, pinned model compatibility, available disk and GPU resources, and run contract self-test against a local golden fixture. It returns structured exit codes and human-readable guidance for remediation.
operator_runbook: - Pre-release: run compat-suite, publish deprecation notices, create release notes with migration steps. - Start rollout: trigger canary to 5% and monitor control-plane dashboard. - Day 0 (canary): verify smoke tests, no error spikes, sanity evals on 10 curated prompts. - Ramp (25%): run longer tail tests and per-customer token cost sanity checks. - Full: mark release 'deployed' in Console and update LTS tags. - Post-deploy: ship release notes, update compatibility matrix.
emergency_patch_process: If a critical security or correctness bug is discovered in production, we can ship a PATCH release to all active channels. PATCHes follow expedited testing: fast-track contract tests and targeted regression suites; rollout uses smaller canary windows but still requires monitoring and automatic rollback thresholds.
observability_and_telemetry: Instrument the runtime to emit: runtime.version, compat.checksum, deprecation.header. Add per-request metadata tags for canary cohorts. Maintain dashboards for errors, p95/p99 latency by cohort, model-accuracy drift metrics from continuous eval jobs, and upgrade-induced token cost deltas.
communication_plan: Publish a 'runtime-compatibility' page in docs with exact deprecation headers and migration examples. Announce breaking changes to subscribed customers and workspace admins via Console and email with at least the minimum window specified in deprecation_policy. Provide a customer-facing FAQ for Dedicated/Private upgrade pathways.
acceptance_criteria: - Documented semver policy published and linked from runtime repo. - rwu CLI MVP capable of preflight and dry-run migration tasks. - Compat-suite executes in CI and blocks merges for MAJOR changes. - Runbook tested in a staged rollout and validated by SRE. - Release notes template includes deprecation headers and migration steps.
